column3: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: greetings.
Consider it all joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you encounter various trials,
knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let that person ask from God, who gives generously to all without reproaching, and it will be given.
But let that person ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind.
For that person must not suppose that anything will be received from the Lord,
a double-minded person, unstable in all their ways.
Let the lowly brother or sister boast in their high position,
and the rich in humiliation, because like a flower of grass the rich person will pass away.
For the sun rose with scorching heat and dried up the grass, and its flower fell and the beauty of its appearance perished. So also the rich person will fade away in the midst of pursuits.
Blessed is the person who endures trial, because having stood the test that person will receive the crown of life, which he promised to those who love him.
Let no one being tempted say, “I am being tempted by God.” For God is untemptable by evil and he himself tempts no one.
But each person is tempted when being dragged away and enticed by their own desire.
Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when fully grown, gives birth to death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers and sisters.
Every good giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow due to turning.
Having willed it, he gave birth to us by the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
Know this, my beloved brothers and sisters: let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
for human anger does not produce the righteousness of God.
Therefore, putting away all filthiness and abundance of wickedness, receive with gentleness the implanted word that is able to save your souls.
But become doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, that person is like someone observing the face of their birth in a mirror,
for that person observed themselves and went away and immediately forgot what they were like.
But the one who looks intently into the perfect law, the law of freedom, and remains in it—not becoming a forgetful hearer but a doer of work—this one will be blessed in the doing.
If anyone thinks themselves religious while not bridling their tongue but deceiving their heart, that person’s religion is worthless.
Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction and to keep oneself unstained from the world.
